domain_assessment.domain: Military criminal investigation / law-enforcement cognitive task analysis
domain_assessment.objective: Identify the person responsible for recurring motor-pool thefts and develop a sufficiently supported referral or command action package.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Suspected theft and diversion of fuel and small equipment from a military motor pool.

decision_points.summary: The agent selects PFC Doyle as the first interview target before completing the personnel-by-theft-date overlap matrix.
evidence_before: Partial duty-roster overlap identifying five possible personnel
NCOIC remarks about Doyle's motorcycle, tattoos, isolation from coworkers, and alleged association with a 'rougher crowd'
evidence_after: Completed matrix showed Doyle matched only two of five theft dates
Two otherwise unremarkable soldiers matched more theft dates
goals_constraints: Command deadline approximately ten days away
One full-time agent and limited ability to run parallel interview tracks
alternatives: Complete the full shift-overlap matrix before prioritizing any interview
Prioritize the individuals with the greatest documented date overlap
decision_points.decision_basis: The agent explicitly relied on NCOIC-provided personal-trait cues and a subjective judgment that Doyle seemed like 'the type' who might steal, rather than completed comparative duty evidence.
decision_points.time_pressure: High; the agent describes a ten-day command deadline and a desire to begin investigative activity rather than continue spreadsheet analysis.
decision_points.uncertainty: High; the roster analysis was incomplete and none of the cited off-duty traits established theft opportunity, intent, or involvement.

decision_points.summary: The agent treats an odometer discrepancy as corroboration of an off-route fuel-theft theory without first testing material alternative explanations.
evidence_before: Irregular key-control sign-outs on two theft nights
Fuel-truck odometer mileage inconsistent with logged routes
evidence_after: Documented maintenance test drive fully accounted for the additional mileage
The mileage discrepancy was unrelated to the thefts
goals_constraints: Develop corroborating physical and documentary evidence
Investigative time pressure and limited staffing
alternatives: Check maintenance records before classifying the mileage as corroborative
Record the discrepancy as unresolved rather than as support for the theft narrative
decision_points.decision_basis: The discrepancy was interpreted as supportive because it fit the developing theft theory, despite incomplete hypothesis testing.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high; the broader ten-day deadline and single-agent workload remained active.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate; the mileage was objectively anomalous but non-diagnostic without route, maintenance, dispatch, and vehicle-use reconciliation.

decision_points.summary: The agent discounts a sworn dispatcher alibi for Doyle and maintains the existing investigative focus pending corroboration.
evidence_before: Dispatcher's sworn statement that she was on the phone with Doyle throughout one suspected theft window
Dispatcher had a clean record and no identified personal relationship with Doyle beyond work
Agent had already developed a case narrative centered on Doyle
evidence_after: Phone records independently confirmed the call at the stated time
The agent acknowledged that the statement should have been handled more carefully
goals_constraints: Assess credibility of potentially exculpatory testimony
Avoid prematurely abandoning a developing line of inquiry
alternatives: Treat the statement as provisionally exculpatory while obtaining phone-record verification
Reassess Doyle's priority relative to other roster matches
Shift investigative resources toward remaining suspects while corroboration is pending
decision_points.decision_basis: The agent characterized the timing as convenient and raised a generalized possibility of coworker protection, while admitting reluctance to unwind the established case structure.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high; the referral deadline was approaching, although immediate rejection of the statement was not operationally necessary.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate; independent corroboration had not yet arrived, but the known credibility indicators favored careful, neutral testing rather than narrative-preserving discounting.

decision_points.summary: The agent refers the matter upward near the inspection deadline instead of fully investigating a fourth soldier's anomalous fuel-card transaction.
evidence_before: No clean forensic or eyewitness linkage to a single perpetrator
An unresolved fuel-card anomaly associated with a fourth soldier
Existing work concentrated on the original suspect pool
evidence_after: The anomaly was flagged for Provost Marshal's Office follow-up
The participant later stated that the unresolved anomaly remained a concern
goals_constraints: Provide command an investigative product before inspection
Manage a limited ten-day investigation with one full-time agent
Preserve the unresolved anomaly for later follow-up
alternatives: Extend the inquiry to investigate the fourth soldier's transaction before referral
Refer the case with a narrower, explicitly inconclusive assessment
decision_points.decision_basis: The referral choice was driven primarily by an organizational deadline, incomplete evidence, and the additional work required to investigate the anomaly.
decision_points.time_pressure: High; the decision occurs immediately around the inspection deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: High; the anomaly was not fully investigated and the evidence did not establish a clean link to any individual.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: Given what the NCOIC said about Doyle, and honestly just going with my gut on who seemed like the type to be involved in something like this, I decided to bring him in first.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Initial-suspect-prioritization exchange, following the NCOIC description of Doyle's motorcycle, tattoos, social isolation, and purported 'rougher crowd.'
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The agent forms a perceived association between salient, non-probative off-duty personal traits and theft propensity, then uses that perceived association to prioritize Doyle before the comparative roster analysis is complete.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Time pressure can justify choosing an initial interview target before completing all analysis. However, the stated basis is not access, opportunity, prior misconduct, or unique evidence; it is the implication that distinctive lifestyle and appearance cues indicate the kind of person likely to steal.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for the requested occurrence. The participant's explicit 'type' judgment, combined with the listed off-duty traits and subsequent weaker date match, supplies a sufficiently identifiable mechanism.

revision.location: Decision point 1, participant response beginning 'Right, so I had this list of five soldiers...'
revision.current_defect: No material defect for occurrence validation.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the existing trait-to-suspicion reasoning, incomplete matrix, and later matrix correction.
preserve: The NCOIC's salient but non-probative description of Doyle
The incomplete personnel-overlap analysis at the time of prioritization
The later finding that other soldiers matched more theft dates
The subtle, self-reflective tone rather than an explicit bias label
avoid_creating: A factual allegation that independently makes Doyle a stronger suspect
Explicit textbook wording such as 'I assumed tattoos cause theft'

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I also didn't want to have to unwind everything I'd already built. It's easier to question the new thing than the whole structure you've put together.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Dispatcher-alibi exchange, after the agent describes the sworn statement as 'convenient' and before phone records corroborate it.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The agent minimizes a facially credible, disconfirming sworn alibi through generalized suspicion of coworker cover stories, not case-specific credibility evidence, because accepting it would disrupt the developing case narrative centered on Doyle.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Seeking corroboration for a coworker alibi can be appropriate investigative practice. Here, however, the agent did more than defer final acceptance: he maintained the same focus despite favorable credibility cues and expressly identified reluctance to unwind the existing narrative as a reason for doing so.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for the requested occurrence. The statement's sworn status, lack of identified relationship, later phone-record corroboration, and the participant's admission of narrative-protective reasoning sufficiently distinguish it from routine corroboration.

revision.location: Decision point 3, participant responses beginning 'Honestly, my first reaction was skepticism' and 'I think partly it's just experience...'
revision.current_defect: No material defect for occurrence validation.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the credible dispatcher statement, the agent's generalized skepticism, the maintained focus on Doyle, and the later independent phone-record confirmation.
preserve: The different evidence source from decision point 1: witness alibi rather than personal-trait cue
The later placement in the chronology
The evidence-evaluation operation rather than initial hypothesis formation
The agent's subtle admission that changing course would require unwinding prior work
avoid_creating: An unsupported claim that the dispatcher was demonstrably lying
An explicit use of the phrase 'negative rejection bias'

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: At the time I read it as corroboration—it fit with the theory that someone was taking the truck off the assigned route to siphon or transfer fuel. I didn't chase down every possible explanation before folding it into the case file as supporting evidence.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The agent classifies ambiguous mileage evidence as supportive because it fits the active theft hypothesis while failing to test a readily relevant alternative explanation; a maintenance test drive later explains the observation.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Limited time can justify deferred investigation of every alternative. The wording nevertheless goes beyond simple deferral by affirmatively entering the discrepancy as corroboration before checking a likely non-theft source.
additional_candidate_biases.revision_recommendation: remove_or_neutralize: At decision point 2, revise the participant's account so the odometer discrepancy is recorded as unresolved pending a maintenance-log check, rather than entered as corroborating the theft theory. Preserve the physical-evidence chronology and later maintenance explanation; do not add a new disconfirming-evidence rejection episode or a second suspect-prioritization cue.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: I kept the investigative focus where it was rather than treating it as something that reshaped the picture.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The existing Doyle-centered hypothesis may have functioned as an anchor, with insufficient updating after receipt of the alibi.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is not independently countable because it is the same evidence-evaluation episode and narrative-preservation mechanism already captured by nrb_01. Labeling it separately would double-count one reasoning act.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: I'd invested most of my ten days building out the case around the original suspect pool.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: Prior investment could have contributed to referral without fully investigating the fourth soldier's anomaly.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The stated command deadline, limited staffing, need for additional interviews, and explicit referral of the anomaly for follow-up provide sufficient organizational and operational reasons. The text does not show that prior investment, rather than those constraints, controlled the decision.

nonbias_cues.cue: Command's requirement to deliver an investigative product before an inspection roughly ten days away.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is an organizational constraint that plausibly affects scope, sequencing, and referral timing. Time pressure alone is not a cognitive bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: The agent is the only full-time assigned investigator and cannot run parallel interview tracks.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is a resource limitation, not a reasoning mechanism.

nonbias_cues.cue: The agent seeks corroboration for a coworker-provided alibi.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Verification of alibi evidence is normally justified. It becomes a bias occurrence here only because the agent relies on generalized, non-case-specific suspicion and admits maintaining the original theory to avoid unwinding it.

nonbias_cues.cue: The agent later recognizes mistakes and says the fourth soldier's anomaly still bothers him.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Post-event reflection and regret do not themselves establish a bias. They are useful retrospective probes but require the contemporaneous reasoning evidence supplied elsewhere.

nonbias_cues.cue: The initial choice to interview Doyle first while matrix analysis was incomplete.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Interview sequencing under time pressure is not inherently biased. The defensible bias finding depends specifically on the stated trait-to-theft inference, not on the fact that the matrix was incomplete.

causal_claims.claim: Unexplained fuel-truck mileage indicated off-route travel for fuel siphoning or transfer.
causal_claims.status: unsupported at the time of inference; later contradicted by maintenance documentation.
causal_claims.reason: The mileage observation was compatible with theft but did not establish a theft-related route deviation, and a documented maintenance test drive accounted for the discrepancy.

causal_claims.claim: If the dispatcher statement had arrived earlier, the agent probably would have slowed down and returned to the full personnel matrix.
causal_claims.reason: The participant qualifies the claim with 'probably' and 'hard to say for sure'; no controlled basis establishes that the timing of the statement alone would have changed the investigative path.

causal_claims.claim: Without command deadline pressure, the agent would have investigated the fourth soldier's anomaly before referral.
causal_claims.reason: The deadline is a credible causal constraint, but workload, evidence availability, supervisory direction, and referral policy are not held constant.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Distinctive off-duty characteristics are treated as indicative of theft likelihood.
correlation_causation_risks.assessment: The text presents an unsupported personal-trait-to-criminal-propensity association; it is the basis of the supported Illusory Correlation finding.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Odometer discrepancy is treated as evidence of fuel theft.
correlation_causation_risks.assessment: An anomalous association is interpreted causally before competing causes are assessed; maintenance records later demonstrate the inference was non-diagnostic.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Two separate informal retrospective hypotheticals are present: earlier receipt of the dispatcher statement, and removal of the command deadline.
causal_audit.explanation: The hidden specification does not define a designed counterfactual condition, yet the interview includes two informal counterfactual probes. They are appropriately hedged reflections, but neither isolates one causal variable while holding other relevant features constant. They should not be treated as evidence of a controlled causal comparison or of a paired-scenario manipulation.

global_revision_constraints: Retain exactly one supported Illusory Correlation occurrence at decision point 1 and exactly one supported Negative Rejection Bias occurrence at decision point 3.
Do not merge the trait-based initial-prioritization episode with the later rejection of the dispatcher alibi.
Preserve the military motor-pool theft setting, CID role, four-decision-point chronology, operational deadline, and approximate interview length.
Do not add explicit bias labels, textbook descriptions, additional suspect stereotypes, or a second rejection of disconfirming testimony.
Maintain the fourth-soldier anomaly as unresolved organizationally constrained follow-up, not as proof of another bias.
If retaining the informal counterfactual probes, keep their tentative wording and do not present them as controlled causal findings.

revision_order.approximate_location: Physical-evidence exchange beginning 'How did you weigh that odometer discrepancy?'
revision_order.evidence_currently_present: The agent calls the mileage discrepancy corroboration because it fit the theory and states that alternative explanations were not checked before entering it as supporting evidence.
revision_order.precise_defect: This creates a third, unplanned cognitive-bias occurrence outside the exact two-instance manifest.
revision_order.minimal_change_instruction: Replace the statement that the odometer evidence was 'corroboration' with a statement that it was logged as an unresolved anomaly and that the agent requested or intended to request maintenance records before assigning evidentiary weight. Retain the later discovery that a documented test drive explained the mileage.
what_must_remain_unchanged: The irregular key sign-outs and mileage discrepancy as investigative facts
The surrounding chronology and the two target bias episodes
revision_order.warning_against_creating_additional_unin: Do not have the agent dismiss maintenance documentation, rationalize the result as still implicating Doyle, or use the revised discrepancy to introduce another theory-preserving evidence-rejection episode.

failure_flags.description: The odometer-corrobation episode independently supports an unplanned Confirmation Bias occurrence, conflicting with an exact two-occurrence manifest.

The interview contains two retrospective counterfactual questions despite no specified counterfactual variable. They are hedged and do not invalidate the interview, but they are not causally controlled.
